caveats: Single app instance: the second ECS task was simulated by editing the rule_configurations row directly in Postgres rather than by a second node calling saveStoredConfiguration; the cache code path exercised is identical.
Reads were driven through the admin GET /api/admin/rule/configuration endpoint, not through a rule evaluation on an HL7 event; both go through RuleService.getConfig and the same LoadingCache.
The red-check log signature is a marker line added to the recompiled pre-fix class so the swap is visible in the log; the original pre-fix code logs nothing on its own.

Guava refreshAfterWrite with the default CacheLoader.reload runs the reload synchronously on the first caller after 30 s, so one rule evaluation per 30 s per (tenant, rule) pays a DB round trip; not measured here, but it is the same cost the old expireAfterAccess load already paid.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: With the rule config read twice a second so the cache entry was never idle, a direct database edit of the stored configuration was picked up by the running app 27.5 s later, inside the 30 s window.
Negative: Reads in between kept serving the cached value, and an edit made through this instance's own admin endpoint still applied instantly.
Red check: With the parent commit's expireAfterAccess RuleService compiled and swapped into the container, the same continuous reads never picked up the database edit in 75 s and the cache loaded exactly once, then the shipped classes were restored and the refresh went green again.

Automation: The merged unit test already covers the regression; one small addition for the local-write-resets-the-window case is proposed.
